note: Facts and sources behind the member descriptions in MI.json, gathered 2026-10-05. "review" holds research notes for a human check; "issues" lists open questions.

byways.name: M-1 Woodward Avenue
byways.where: M-1 (Woodward Avenue) from Hart Plaza on the Detroit River northwest to Pontiac, about 27 miles; Wayne and Oakland counties

facts.fact: Woodward Avenue follows, in part, the route of a Native American trail from Detroit to Pontiac; the byway runs 27 miles from Hart Plaza to Pontiac.
The Ford Piquette Avenue Plant, Ford's first built factory, is where the first 12,000 Model Ts were produced.
The 16-mile Oakland County stretch hosts the Woodward Dream Cruise of classic cars on the third Saturday of August.
WA3 describes the historic Woodward Corridor as 27 miles long.

byways.review: Official page is the Woodward Avenue Action Association (WA3), the byway organization.

byways.name: US-41 Copper Country Trail
byways.where: US-41 from the Portage Lake Lift Bridge in Hancock to Copper Harbor, with spurs on M-203, M-26, Brockway Mountain Drive and Cliff Drive; Houghton and Keweenaw counties

facts.fact: The byway runs from the Portage Lake Lift Bridge in Hancock to Copper Harbor and follows the copper lode of the Keweenaw Peninsula.
The M-26 spur passes the Quincy Smelting Works, described as the nation's last remaining 19th-century smelting works.
Brockway Mountain Drive near Copper Harbor gives a panoramic view of forested mountains and Lake Superior and is maintained seasonally.
The byway organization describes the route from Hancock and Houghton to Calumet through Copper Harbor.

byways.name: M-65 River Road
byways.where: River Road from M-65 north of Hale east to US-23 at Oscoda, about 22 miles; Iosco County, Huron National Forest

facts.fact: The 22-mile byway runs west from Lake Huron into the Huron National Forest, paralleling the Au Sable River, once a route for floating white pine to Lake Huron sawmills.
Lumberman's Monument is a 14-foot bronze statue of three lumbermen above the Au Sable River.
At Iargo Springs a 300-step staircase, boardwalks and an overlook were built in 1991.
The Forest Service describes the twenty-two mile River Road National Scenic Byway as paralleling the historic Riviere aux Sable.

byways.review: MDOT lists it as 'M-65 River Road'; the byway itself is River Road (Iosco County) between M-65 and US-23, also a USFS forest byway. USFS page is the forest's Scenic Drives page, which describes it.

byways.name: Whitefish Bay National Forest
byways.where: Lakeshore Drive (Curley Lewis Memorial Highway) from Brimley and the Bay Mills Indian Community west to M-123 south of Paradise, about 33 miles; Chippewa County, Hiawatha National Forest

facts.fact: The byway runs from the Bay Mills Indian Community through the Hiawatha National Forest to M-123 south of Paradise; it is also named the I.L. 'Curley' Lewis Memorial Highway.
From the Mission Hill/Spectacle Lake overlook travelers can see the Point Iroquois Lighthouse tower and freighters heading for the Soo Locks.
Lake Shore Drive passes northern hardwoods, conifers and wetlands; visitors can climb the Point Iroquois Lighthouse tower.

byways.review: USFS designation, but MDOT lists it as one of the 22 Pure Michigan Byways.

byways.name: Black River National Forest
byways.where: CR 513 (Black River Road) from Bessemer north to Black River Harbor on Lake Superior; Gogebic County, Ottawa National Forest

facts.fact: By 1904 the State of Michigan had built a wagon road from Bessemer to Lake Superior; that road is now the Black River Scenic Byway.
Five waterfalls (Great Conglomerate, Potawatomi, Gorge, Sandstone and Rainbow) lie along the final 3 miles of the byway, reached by trails and stairs.
Copper Peak, ten miles north of Bessemer, rises 364 feet beside the byway and holds the Copper Peak Ski Flying Hill.
The Forest Service says the byway runs 11 miles from CR 204 and CR 513 to Black River Harbor and was dedicated on September 19, 1992.

byways.review: USFS designation listed by MDOT among the 22. Length differs: MDOT guide says 15 miles from Bessemer, USFS says 11 miles from CR 204.

byways.name: M-22 Byway
byways.where: M-22 from M-72 at Traverse City around the Leelanau Peninsula (with M-204 and M-109 connectors) and south through Benzie and Manistee counties to US-31, 116 miles

facts.fact: M-22 was built in 1913 as the first state highway in Leelanau, Benzie and Manistee counties; the byway is 116 miles.
Leland's Fishtown is a working fishing village with weathered shanties, smokehouses and fish tugs along the Leland River.
The byway passes Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore with dunes about 450 feet tall, and orchards and vineyards along the shore.
Point Betsie Lighthouse, built in 1858, still marks the southern entrance to the Manitou Passage.

byways.name: M-37 Old Mission Peninsula
byways.where: M-37 (Center Road) from Traverse City north to Mission Point, 18 miles; Peninsula Township, Grand Traverse County

facts.fact: The first public road in Grand Traverse County was built in 1853 from Traverse City to Old Mission; in 1935 it was named 'Queen's Highway' for the cherry festival queen.
The byway runs 18 miles through orchards, vineyards and farms with views of both arms of Grand Traverse Bay.
Mission Point Lighthouse, completed in 1870, stands on the 45th parallel at the end of the peninsula.

byways.review: No byway website found; MDOT links only a Networks Northwest corridor plan folder.

byways.name: M-119 Tunnel of Trees
byways.where: M-119 from Harbor Springs north to Cross Village, about 20 miles; Emmet County

facts.fact: The 20.5-mile route follows the Lake Michigan bluffs from Harbor Springs through Good Hart to Cross Village.
In 1936 Alice Irwin led a successful petition to the Legislature to preserve the road in its natural state; it still has no shoulders or centerline.
The Good Hart General Store, built in 1934, is still a general store and post office.
The byway committee calls it a Scenic Heritage Route spanning roughly 20 miles of M-119.

byways.review: Catalog marks this road 'Classic drive (not a designated scenic byway)', but MDOT lists it as a State Scenic Byway; the catalog designation should be corrected.

byways.name: M-123 Tahquamenon
byways.where: M-123 from M-28 at Newberry north and east through Paradise to M-28 at Eckerman, 63 miles; Luce and Chippewa counties

facts.fact: The byway is a 63-mile route between the M-28/M-123 intersections at Newberry and Eckerman.
The Upper Tahquamenon Falls drops about 50 feet and spans 200 feet, with dark tannin-colored water, amid Michigan's largest stand of old growth.
The Tahquamenon Rivermouth unit lies where the river meets Whitefish Bay.
M-123 was first designated a Michigan Scenic Heritage Route in 1997 from Galloway Creek to County Road 500, later expanded to all of M-123.

byways.name: US-2 Top of the Lake
byways.where: US-2 from St. Ignace west to Manistique, 92 miles; Mackinac and Schoolcraft counties

facts.fact: For 92 miles US-2 follows the northern shore of Lake Michigan from St. Ignace to Manistique, built on traces of an ancient Native American trade route.
The road winds along tall bluffs and dives down to skirt miles of deserted beaches.
The Cut River Bridge, on the National Register of Historic Places, has trails and stairways down into the gorge and under its trusses.

byways.review: The byway's own site topofthelake.org did not respond; the EUP regional planning commission page is used instead. MDOT guide text mentions Thompson as the west end but its planning tips say Manistique.

byways.name: US-23 Sunrise Coast
byways.where: US-23 along Lake Huron from Standish to Mackinaw City, 200 miles; Arenac, Iosco, Alcona, Alpena, Presque Isle and Cheboygan counties

facts.fact: The Lake Huron Shores Good Roads Association finished the Huron Shores Highway, now US-23, in 1913.
The 200-mile route runs from the historic train depot in Standish to Mackinaw City and passes 16 lighthouses.
Thunder Bay National Marine Sanctuary at Alpena protects more than 200 shipwrecks.

byways.review: Formerly the US-23 Heritage Route; heritage23.com now redirects to sunrisecoast.org.

byways.name: I-69 Recreational
byways.where: I-69 from the Indiana line north through Branch and Calhoun counties to the Eaton County line, 80 miles

facts.fact: The route extends from the Michigan/Indiana border north along I-69 through Branch and Calhoun counties to the Eaton County border, 80 miles.
Branch County has more than 100 inland lakes and sells more fishing licenses than any other Michigan county.
Coldwater's Tibbits Opera House, built in 1882, is one of the oldest theaters in Michigan.

byways.name: M-15 Pathway to Family Fun
byways.where: M-15 from US-24 at Clarkston north to Bay City, 74 miles; Oakland, Genesee, Lapeer, Tuscola and Bay counties

facts.fact: The byway runs from the US-24 junction near Clarkston to Bay City as a family-friendly alternative to I-75; it is 74 miles.
North of Clarkston the route narrows to two lanes through rural countryside and farmland, with inland lakes near Ortonville.
The M-15 Yard Sale is held from Clarkston to Vassar on the first Saturday of May each year.

byways.review: Official page is the East Michigan Council of Governments byway page.

byways.name: M-35 Hidden Coast
byways.where: M-35 from US-41 at Menominee north along Green Bay and Little Bay de Noc through Escanaba to US-2 at Gladstone, 64 miles; Menominee and Delta counties

facts.fact: The byway runs 64 miles between Menominee and Gladstone along Lake Michigan's northwestern shore, over large parts of the old Native American Sault and Green Bay Trail.
The West Shore Fishing Museum in Bailey Park, 13 miles north of Menominee, is in the restored house of the Charles L. Bailey commercial fishery.
Escanaba's Sand Point Lighthouse has been restored to its 1868 working condition.

byways.name: Chief Noonday
byways.where: M-179 (Chief Noonday Road) from US-131 at Bradley east to M-43 west of Hastings, 17 miles; Allegan and Barry counties

facts.fact: M-179, also known as Chief Noonday Road, runs 17 miles east from US-131 at Bradley to M-43 near Hastings under a canopy of hardwoods.
Noahquageshik, or Chief Noonday, of the Ottawas (Odawas) lived on the Grand River in the early to mid-1800s and spent his last years in the Yankee Springs area.
Yankee Springs Recreation Area covers 5,200 acres with nine lakes and Devil's Soupbowl, a glacially carved kettle.

byways.name: M-134 North Huron
byways.where: M-134 from I-75 exit 359 east along Lake Huron through Hessel, Cedarville and DeTour, then by ferry to Drummond Island, 50 miles; Mackinac and Chippewa counties

facts.fact: The 50-mile route begins at I-75 exit 359 and ends on Drummond Island; drive time excludes the ferry.
The Les Cheneaux Islands are 36 small islands along 12 miles of Lake Huron shoreline.
DeTour village offers views of freighters in the St. Mary's River and DeTour Passage.
The North Huron Scenic Byway was designated in 2015 and runs from I-75 to Four Corners on Drummond Island.

byways.review: The MDOT guide calls it the North Huron Recreational Trail; the EUP commission calls it the North Huron Scenic Byway.

byways.name: US-31 West Michigan Pike
byways.where: I-94/I-94 BL, M-63, I-196/US-31 and business routes from the Indiana line at New Buffalo north through St. Joseph, South Haven, Holland, Grand Haven and Muskegon to US-10 near Ludington, 184 miles

facts.fact: The 184-mile West Michigan Pike, now US-31, is described by MDOT as the first paved road in Michigan built especially for visitors.
The route runs from the state line near New Buffalo to the US-31/US-10 intersection near Ludington.
Silver Lake Sand Dunes near Hart allow off-road vehicle rides to the tops of the dunes.
Michigan Beachtowns describes the Pike as a historic byway connecting the beach towns.

byways.name: US-12 Heritage Trail
byways.where: US-12 (Michigan Avenue) from Woodward Avenue in downtown Detroit west through Ypsilanti, the Irish Hills, Coldwater, Sturgis and Niles to the Indiana line near New Buffalo, 208 miles

facts.fact: US-12 follows an early Native American trail known to European settlers as the Sauk Trail; in 1994 the Legislature named it the 'Iron Brigade' Memorial Highway.
The road winds through the lake-dotted Irish Hills, including Wampler's Lake in Walter J. Hayes State Park.
The 1922 St. Joseph River/Mottville Bridge is the longest surviving reinforced concrete camelback bridge in Michigan.
The byway runs 208 miles from M-1 in Detroit to the Indiana line near New Buffalo.

byways.name: US-2 Iron County Heritage Trail
byways.where: US-2, M-69 and CR 424 between Crystal Falls and Iron River; Iron County

facts.fact: The trail links 14 sites between Crystal Falls and Iron River, all within Iron County.
The Iron County Courthouse sits at the top of downtown Crystal Falls.
Larson Park on US-2 is thought to be the first roadside park in the nation.

byways.review: Length uncertain: MDOT guide says 16 miles, MDOT GIS DrivingDistance says 36. ironheritage.org is now an unrelated site, do not use.

byways.name: I-94 Marshall's Territorial Road
byways.where: Michigan Avenue (I-94 Business Loop) through the city of Marshall, 1.2 miles; Calhoun County

facts.fact: The Marshall Historic District, a National Historic Landmark district, has more than 850 buildings including the Honolulu House.
The Governor's Mansion was built in 1839 in the hope it would house the governor if Marshall became the state capital.
The Honolulu House, built in 1860 by Abner Pratt, stands north of Fountain Circle and blends Italianate, Polynesian and Gothic Revival styles.
The byway is 1.2 miles long.

byways.review: MDOT names it 'I-94 Marshall's Territorial Road', but the byway is Michigan Avenue inside Marshall, not the interstate.

byways.name: M-15 and M-25 Center Avenue/Bay City
byways.where: M-25 (Center Avenue) from Madison Avenue in downtown Bay City east to Livingston Street, 1.5 miles; Bay County

facts.fact: The byway runs 1.5 miles on Center Avenue (M-25) from Madison Avenue east to Livingston Street.
Lumber barons built Victorian mansions on broad lawns along the tree-lined street from the early 1870s; Italianate and Queen Anne styles are prominent.
The Center Avenue Neighborhood Residential District has almost 900 historic structures.

byways.review: MDOT's table name mentions M-15, but the guide and GIS describe only Center Avenue (M-25); M-15 is the separate Pathway to Family Fun byway that ends here.

byways.name: M-125 Monroe Street
byways.where: M-125 (Monroe Street) through the city of Monroe across the River Raisin, about 2 miles; Monroe County

facts.fact: About 40 historic sites lie along 2 miles of Monroe Street; Monroe became the first Michigan city to receive a Heritage Route designation, in early 1996.
The George Armstrong Custer Equestrian Monument, a 14-foot bronze, stands at Monroe Street and Elm Avenue.
The River Raisin National Battlefield Park preserves a War of 1812 battlefield near the byway at East Elm Avenue and Dixie Highway.

byways.review: Catalog line maps about 6.8 miles, but MDOT describes a 2-mile byway; catalog designation 'Michigan State Scenic Byway' should read State Historic Byway.

issues: michigan.gov blocks curl and WebFetch (Akamai 403 'Access Denied' even with the project User-Agent); the program table and the 30 MB driving guide PDF were read through the browser. Every fact citing the guide PDF comes from that browser read.
Catalog road tunnel-of-trees-m-119-980005 is marked 'Classic drive (not a designated scenic byway)', but MDOT lists M-119 Tunnel of Trees as a State Scenic Byway; its designation should be updated.

Catalog monroe-street-m125-13755 maps about 6.8 miles and is labeled 'Michigan State Scenic Byway'; MDOT describes a 2-mile State Historic Byway on Monroe Street. Check the catalog line against the MDOT GIS feature 'Monroe Street'.
Catalog woodward and copper country entries still carry the old 'Michigan Heritage Route' label; the program has been called Pure Michigan Byways since 2014.
Black River length disagrees: MDOT guide 15 miles from Bessemer, USFS 11 miles from CR 204 (catalog 11.3).
Iron County Heritage Trail length disagrees: guide says 16 miles, MDOT GIS DrivingDistance says 36. The domain ironheritage.org is now an unrelated site.
Proposed M-55 Recreational Heritage Route (Manistee to Tawas City) appears in an MDOT StoryMap from 2023 but not in MDOT's list of 22 designated byways; treated as not designated.

US-2 Top of the Lake: topofthelake.org did not respond (connection failure and 502); the EUP planning page is used. The guide text mentions Thompson as the west end while its planning tips and the EUP page say Manistique.
MDOT table name 'M-15 and M-25 Center Avenue/Bay City' covers only Center Avenue (M-25) in the guide and GIS.

No official page found for Old Mission Peninsula, I-69 Recreational, Hidden Coast, Chief Noonday, Iron County Heritage Trail, Marshall's Territorial Road, Center Avenue/Bay City and Monroe Street; url is null. Web search budget was exhausted, so a further search for these could turn something up.
Corridor plan links in MDOT's table use http (m119tunneloftrees.org/learn.asp, m22byway.org/plans.asp, emcog.org); https versions of the byway home pages were used instead.
